The tools a connection sees depend on its level ([Keys](/docs/build/keys-and-scopes/)). Descriptions are the server's own words; the parameter tables come from `vault-info { "help": "<tool>" }`.

| Tool | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `query-records` | read | Read records: one record, a filtered list, a search, a link neighbourhood or path, counts, or a record's history. |
| `create-record` | write | Create a record, or several with `records: [...]`. `types` names its types (existing types or new names); `tags` adds labels. If `path` is taken, `if_exists` decides: error (default), ignore, update (merge into it) or replace. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "create-record"}. If no existing type fits what the record is, name a new type for it rather than using the nearest one. |
| `update-record` | write | Change a record (id, path or title), or several with `records: [{id, …}]`. |
| `delete-record` | write | Delete a record (by id, path or title), with its tags and links. |
| `list-types` | read | Every type and tag with its `kind` and counts (`count` exact, `expanded_count` with subtypes). `name` gives one in full (fields, parents); `include_schema: true` gives all of them. |
| `vault-info` | read | The vault's description, types and their fields, indexed fields, and counts (`include_stats`). `help: "<tool>"` returns a tool's full reference. Admins may set `description`. |
| `docs` | read | Parachute's how-to pages, as markdown. No `topic`: the list; `topic`: one page. |
| `doctor` | read | Read-only check of types, tags and fields (dangling parents, cycles, a field holding two data types, a field that names records but isn't a reference, names one letter apart). Returns findings, each with a remedy; fixes nothing. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "doctor"}. |
| `read-attachment` | read | Read an attachment into the conversation: text in byte slices, images as images. |
| `attachment-url` | read | A one-use URL for an attachment's bytes. upload: `record`, `filename` and exact `size_bytes`, then PUT the bytes to `url`. download: `attachment_id` (from query-records `include_attachments: true`). Every parameter: vault-info {help: "attachment-url"}. |
| `manage-types` | admin | Change the vault's types and tags. `action`: update (default: create or change one; `fields` and `parent_names` make it a type), rename {old_name, new_name}, merge {sources, target}, delete {tag, detach?}, prune (drop unused indexed columns), migrate {tag, field, transform} (change a field's values, e.g. before a retype); both a dry run unless `apply: true`. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "manage-types"}. |
| `manage-keys` | admin | Mint, list or revoke short-lived keys for this vault. mint: `scope` (e.g. "vault:home:read"), `ttl_seconds` (default 900, max 3600, or 90 days with `long_lived: true`), `name`, `description`. revoke: `name` or `jti`. Minted keys can't exceed yours. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "manage-keys"}. |

Still answering, and going in 1.0: `query-notes`, `create-note`, `update-note`, `delete-note`, `list-tags`, `find-path`, `update-tag`, `rename-tag`, `merge-tags`, `delete-tag`, `prune-schema`, `request-attachment-upload`, `request-attachment-download`, `manage-token`. Each says what replaced it.

## query-records

Read records: one record, a filtered list, a search, a link neighbourhood or path, counts, or a record's history.
- One record: `id` (id, path or title). Lists leave the body out unless `include_body: true`.
- Filters combine (AND). `type` matches a type and its subtypes (by `parent_names`; a `/` in a name only files it); `tag` matches a label. `fields` operators work on any field: an indexed one (vault-info lists them) is fastest, any other is read in full and the reply warns `scan`.
- Each record has `types` (what it is), `tags` (labels), `fields` and a `body`.
- Returns an array of records, or `{records, next_cursor?, warnings?}` with `cursor` or warnings, or `[{group, value}]` with `aggregate`. An empty page means done.
- `search`: a question in plain words ("when did I write about…", "have we decided…") is ranked by keyword and meaning together when the vault has meaning search and its auto setting is on (the default); 1–3 words (a name, an id) match exactly. `search_mode: "literal"` forces exact words.
Rarer filters (has_links, order_by, expand_links, created_by, …) are accepted too. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "query-records"}.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Get one record by ID, path, or (fallback, only when id/path both miss and exactly one record matches) its H1 title |
| `tag` | string or array | Filter by tag(s) |
| `type` | string or array | Type(s), subtypes included |
| `tag_match` | string | How to match multiple tags: 'any' (OR, default) or 'all' (AND) |
| `exclude_tags` | string or array | Exclude records with these tag(s). Accepts a single tag or an array. Aliases `excludeTags` and `exclude_tag` are also accepted. If multiple alias forms are provided, `exclude_tags` takes precedence (then `excludeTags`, then `exclude_tag`). |
| `path` | string | Exact path match (case-insensitive) |
| `path_prefix` | string | Path prefix match (e.g., 'Projects/') |
| `search` | string | Full-text search query, matched against a record's title (path), its content and its field values — a title match ranks far above a passing body mention, and a field-only match comes after title and body matches. (vault#551): your text is escaped and phrase-quoted before reaching FTS5, so punctuation ("didn't", "eleven-day", "18.6") is matched as literal content rather than parsed as FTS5 query sy |
| `search_mode` | string | How `search` text is turned into an FTS5 query (vault#551). "literal": escape + phrase-quote the text so punctuation is literal content, not FTS5 syntax — the fix for `search: "didn't"` / "eleven-day" / "18.6" silently returning `[]`. "advanced": pass the text through to FTS5 raw, for callers who want boolean (AND/OR/NOT), manual phrase quoting, or prefix (`*`) syntax — a malformed advanced query  |
| `fields` | object | Filter by fields values. Each value is either a primitive (exact match by JSON type, so `{done: true}` and `{streak: 4}` find a stored boolean and number; a stored string that reads the same also matches, but a string filter like `{streak: "4"}` finds only the string) or an operator object: `{eq\|ne\|gt\|gte\|lt\|lte\|in\|not_in\|exists: value}`. Operator objects require the field to be declared ` |
| `since` | string | What changed since then: records made OR edited at or after this time (ISO). Shorthand for `date_filter: { field: 'updated_at', from }`. For only the records made since then, use `date_from`. |
| `date_from` | string | Start date (ISO, inclusive). Filters on `created_at` (vault ingestion time), so it misses edits to older records; for what changed, use `since`. Shorthand for `date_filter: { field: 'created_at', from }`. |
| `date_to` | string | End date (ISO, exclusive). Filters on `created_at` (vault ingestion time). Shorthand for `date_filter: { field: 'created_at', to }`. |
| `date_filter` | object | Generalized date-range filter. Use this when the date that matters is the *content* date (e.g. an email's received date, a meeting's scheduled date) rather than the vault ingestion time, or when paging by `updated_at` for incremental rebuilds. Mutually exclusive with the top-level `date_from` / `date_to` shorthand. |
| `near` | object | Scope results to records within N hops of an anchor record. Composes with `aggregate` (rollup over the neighborhood). A tag-scoped token cannot anchor on a record it cannot see. |
| `aggregate` | object | Aggregation / rollup mode. Omit `group_by` with `op: "count"` for a filtered total (`[{group: null, value: N}]`, including |

Deleted-record history is also unavailable to unscoped MCP sessions; restore is REST-only. |

Slices end on a UTF-8 codepoint boundary, so a slice may be  |

## create-record

Create a record, or several with `records: [...]`. `types` names its types (existing types or new names); `tags` adds labels. If `path` is taken, `if_exists` decides: error (default), ignore, update (merge into it) or replace. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "create-record"}. If no existing type fits what the record is, name a new type for it rather than using the nearest one.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `body` | string | Record content (markdown). Wikilinks like [[Target]] auto-resolve. |
| `path` | string | Record path (e.g., 'Projects/README') |
| `extension` | string | File extension (vault#328). Default "md". Use "csv"/"yaml"/"json"/"mdx"/etc. for non-markdown records. Lowercase alphanumeric, 1–16 chars; no '.' or '/'. The "parachute" prefix is reserved. |
| `tags` | array | Tags to apply |
| `types` | array | Types; land with the tags |
| `fields` | object | Fields fields |
| `links` | array | Links to create from this record. `target` resolves with the SAME semantics as a [[wikilink]] (vault#555) — ID, then exact path, then basename, then (only on a clean miss, and only when exactly one record matches) an H1-title fallback. A target created LATER in the same `records` batch, or by a future call, resolves automatically (queued + backfilled) — the response carries an `unresolved_link` wa |
| `created_at` | string | ISO timestamp (defaults to now) |
| `if_exists` | string | What to do when `path` already names an existing record (vault#555). See the tool description for the full contract of each mode. Default "error" — unchanged path_conflict behavior. |
| `records` | array | Array of records for batch creation |
| `summary` | boolean | Batch calls only (a `records` array): return a compact `{created, ids, failed}` shape instead of N full record objects. See the tool description. Ignored on a single-record call. |

## update-record

Change a record (id, path or title), or several with `records: [{id, …}]`.
- Body: `body` (replace all), `append`/`prepend`, or `body_edit` (old_text must occur once).
- `fields` merges (null deletes a key); `types`/`tags`/`links` take {add, remove}.
- Except append/prepend, pass `if_updated_at` (the updated_at you read) or `force: true`.
- `if_missing: "create"` makes the record if missing. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "update-record"}.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Record ID, path, or (fallback, only when id/path both miss and exactly one record matches) its H1 title |
| `body` | string | New content (full replace). Mutually exclusive with `append`/`prepend` and `body_edit`. |
| `append` | string | Text to append to the end of the record. Atomic at the SQL layer — concurrent appends are safe. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `body_edit`. No precondition required. |
| `prepend` | string | Text to prepend to the start of the record. Atomic at the SQL layer. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `body_edit`. May combine with `append`. No precondition required. |
| `body_edit` | object | Find-and-replace one occurrence. Errors if `old_text` is not found or matches multiple locations. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `append`/`prepend`. |
| `fields` | object | Fields to merge (keys are merged, not replaced wholesale). A value of `null` deletes that key (RFC 7386 merge-patch) — e.g. `{"new_key": "v", "old_key": null}` renames in one call. Omitting a key preserves its existing value. |
| `tags` | object | Tags to add/remove |
| `types` | object | {add, remove}, as tags |
| `links` | object | Links to add/remove. `add[].target` resolves with the SAME semantics as a [[wikilink]] (vault#555) — ID, then exact path, then basename, then (only on a clean miss, and only when exactly one record matches) an H1-title fallback — and lazily backfills (queued) when the target arrives later; the response carries an `unresolved_link` warning naming the target in the meantime, never a silent drop. |
| `path` | string | New path |
| `if_updated_at` | string | Optimistic concurrency check: the updated_at value you last read. Rejects with a conflict error if the record has been modified since. Required unless `force: true` is set or the call is `append`/`prepend`-only. |
| `force` | boolean | Waive the *requirement to supply* `if_updated_at` and run the update unconditionally. Use only for bulk migrations or scripted writes where concurrency is known-safe. Record: this does not override an `if_updated_at` you actually pass — if you supply both, the precondition still applies and a mismatch returns a conflict error. |
| `if_missing` | string | What to do when the record (by `id`/path) doesn't exist. `"fail"` (default) — error, current behavior. `"create"` — create the record from this same payload (content/path/tags/fields become the create fields; the response carries `created: true`). Skips the `if_updated_at` precondition on the create branch (nothing to conflict with). Idempotent for sync loops that don't know ahead of time whether  |
| `records` | array | Array of record updates for batch |
| `extension` | string | Change the record's file extension (vault#328). Allowed but caller-owned — you're responsible for content validity if you switch a non-empty record's extension. Lowercase alphanumeric, 1–16 chars; "parachute" prefix reserved. |
| `created_at` | string | New created_at timestamp |
| `state_transition` | object | Atomic compare-and-set state transition (vault#299). If the fields `field` currently equals `from`, set it to `to` and commit; otherwise the write is rejected with a `transition_conflict` error (a missing field counts as a conflict; `from: null` matches absent-or-null). A transition-ONLY update needs no `if_updated_at`/`force` — the compare-and-set is the precondition. Combinable with other field  |
| `include_content` | boolean | Response shape opt-out. Default `true` (returns the full Record with content). Set `false` to receive the lean index shape (drops `body`, adds `byteSize`, a whitespace-collapsed `preview`, and a computed `displayTitle`). `validation_status` is preserved on the lean shape when present. Applies uniformly to single and batch responses. |
| `include_links` | boolean | Echo the record's hydrated inbound + outbound links on the response (vault feedback #8). Links are *also* echoed automatically whenever the update itself mutated links (`links.add`/`links.remove`), so you rarely need to set this — its purpose is to fetch the current link set on an update that didn't touch links. Default: `false` (and absent from the response unless mutated or requested). Mirrors ` |

## delete-record

Delete a record (by id, path or title), with its tags and links.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Record ID, path, or (fallback, only when id/path both miss and exactly one record matches) its H1 title |
| `ids` | array | Several records (IDs or paths), instead of `id`; up to 500 |
| `erase_history` | boolean | Also erase every saved version, so the vault can't restore the record (default false; a git mirror or backup keeps its own copy). Needs admin scope. Takes only an exact id or path. |

## list-types

Every type and tag with its `kind` and counts (`count` exact, `expanded_count` with subtypes). `name` gives one in full (fields, parents); `include_schema: true` gives all of them.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Get details for a single tag |
| `include_schema` | boolean | Include full tag record (description, fields, relationships, parent_names, timestamps) for each tag (default: false) |

## vault-info

The vault's description, types and their fields, indexed fields, and counts (`include_stats`). `help: "<tool>"` returns a tool's full reference. Admins may set `description`.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `include_stats` | boolean | Include note count, tag count, attachment/link counts, and the monthly note distribution (default: false) |
| `help` | string | A tool name |
| `description` | string | If provided, updates the vault description |

Parachute's how-to pages, as markdown. No `topic`: the list; `topic`: one page.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|

## doctor

Read-only check of types, tags and fields (dangling parents, cycles, a field holding two data types, a field that names records but isn't a reference, names one letter apart). Returns findings, each with a remedy; fixes nothing. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "doctor"}.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `deep` | boolean | Opt-in, unrestricted sessions only: materialize and hash-check a bounded history blob page. Check history_audit.complete; incomplete is not a clean audit. |
| `history_after` | string | Resume after history_audit.next_after. Pages are not a snapshot; audit a consistent backup for snapshot assurance. |
| `history_max_blobs` | integer | Maximum blobs in a deep page; default 100. |
| `history_budget_ms` | integer | Between-blob budget; default 250ms. One blob may exceed it. |

## read-attachment

Read an attachment into the conversation: text in byte slices, images as images.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `attachment_id` | string | The attachment's id (from a note's attachment rows, e.g. include_attachments: true on query-notes) |
| `content_offset` | number | Text attachments only. Byte offset to start reading from (UTF-8 bytes). Defaults to 0. |
| `content_length` | number | Text attachments only. Byte budget for this call. Defaults to 65536 (64 KiB); max 262144 (256 KiB). |

## attachment-url

A one-use URL for an attachment's bytes. upload: `record`, `filename` and exact `size_bytes`, then PUT the bytes to `url`. download: `attachment_id` (from query-records `include_attachments: true`). Every parameter: vault-info {help: "attachment-url"}.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | upload, download |
| `record` | string | upload: record id or path |
| `filename` | string |  |
| `size_bytes` | number |  |
| `mime_type` | string |  |
| `transcribe` | boolean | Audio: transcribe it |
| `attachment_id` | string | download |

Actions: `upload`, `download`.

## manage-types

Change the vault's types and tags. `action`: update (default: create or change one; `fields` and `parent_names` make it a type), rename {old_name, new_name}, merge {sources, target}, delete {tag, detach?}, prune (drop unused indexed columns), migrate {tag, field, transform} (change a field's values, e.g. before a retype); both a dry run unless `apply: true`. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "manage-types"}.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | update, rename, merge, delete, prune, migrate |
| `tag` | string |  |
| `kind` | string | type: has fields/parents; tag: a flat label |
| `description` | string |  |
| `fields` | object | {name: {type: "string"\|"integer"\|"number"\|"boolean"\|"date"\|"reference", enum?, indexed?, default?, required?, strict?, cardinality?, target_tags?}}. reference: points at a record (target_tags: its types). required: should be set (refused only if strict). strict: refuse a wrong value. cardinality "many": a list. |
| `parent_names` | array |  |
| `old_name` | string |  |
| `new_name` | string |  |
| `sources` | array |  |
| `target` | string |  |
| `detach` | boolean |  |
| `field` | string |  |
| `transform` | object | {kind: "to_string"\|"to_int"\|"remap"\|…} |
| `continue_on_error` | boolean |  |
| `apply` | boolean |  |
| `force` | boolean |  |

Actions: `update`, `rename`, `merge`, `delete`, `prune`, `migrate`.

## manage-keys

Mint, list or revoke short-lived keys for this vault. mint: `scope` (e.g. "vault:home:read"), `ttl_seconds` (default 900, max 3600, or 90 days with `long_lived: true`), `name`, `description`. revoke: `name` or `jti`. Minted keys can't exceed yours. Every parameter: vault-info {help: "manage-keys"}.

| Parameter | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | Which action to perform. Required. |
| `scope` | string or array | (action=mint) Scope to grant. String like "vault:write" or array. Must be a subset of the caller's scope; cross-vault scopes are rejected. |
| `ttl_seconds` | number | (action=mint) Token lifetime in seconds. Default 900 (15 min), max 3600 (1 hour); with long_lived=true, max 7776000 (90 days). Values outside the applicable (0, max] range are rejected. |
| `long_lived` | boolean | (action=mint, optional) Set true to raise the TTL cap from 1 hour to 90 days. A 90-day token is a standing credential: long-lived and meaningfully increases blast radius if leaked/misused. |
| `description` | string | (action=mint, optional) Free-text label surfaced in the token list + audit trail. |
| `name` | string | (action=mint, optional) The key's name: its writes are stamped `via key:<name>`, and revoke takes the name. Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; one key per name, forever. |
| `jti` | string | (action=revoke) The jti (e.g. `t_abc123…`) returned by a prior mint. Revoke is idempotent — second revoke also returns ok=true. |
